subject: Re: MSA redlines — consequential damages / mutuality
messages:
From: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@datastrm.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA redlines — consequential damages / mutuality

Hi Vivek / Laura,

Thanks for sending the draft MSA. Attached are DataStream's redlines (DataStream_MSA_Redlines_v2.pdf). Our core ask on Section 10 (Limitation of Liability) is that the consequential damages exclusion be mutual. Specifically, we propose: 

  "Neither party shall be liable to the other for any consequential, incidental, special, exemplary or punitive damages, including lost profits, loss of business, or loss of data, arising out of or related to this Agreement, regardless of the cause of action."

We understand redwood's standard is typically a one-way exclusion (customer's consequential damages recoverable). The mutual exclusion is important for our procurement team given the way we integrate third-party inference providers into our stack — particularly where downstream losses (third-party integrations) are concerned.

If mutuality is a hard no, can you confirm at minimum a carve-out for gross negligence, willful misconduct, breach of confidentiality, and IP indemnity-triggered damages? We also flagged the definition of "consequential" — our counsel prefers a plain list (lost profits, business interruption, loss of data, loss of customers) rather than a residual-definition.

Would appreciate a quick read and a suggested counter if necessary. We have a procurement window next week.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Bennett
Lead Counsel, DataStream Analytics
legal@datastrm.com

-- Attachment: DataStream_MSA_Redlines_v2.pdf (PDF; 12 pages)

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@datastrm.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — consequential damages / mutuality

Sarah —

Thanks for the redlines and the clear ask. Quick answer up-front: Redwood's standard position on consequential damages is a one-way exclusion (i.e., Redwood excludes consequential damages but remains liable for direct damages to customers). The why is practical and commercial — we need to be able to make customers whole for direct costs if the service materially fails, while keeping catastrophic downstream exposure priced out of our platform economics.

That said, we are open to a narrow compromise that preserves our commercial protections but provides DataStream the assurances it needs. Proposed middle ground:

  1) Keep a one-way exclusion but expand the carve-outs so that the exclusion does not apply to: (a) breaches of confidentiality; (b) Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct; (c) damages arising under the IP indemnity; and (d) losses demonstrably caused by Redwood's failure to follow a mutually agreed SLA in the Order Form.

  2) Narrow the definition list for consequential to the commonly agreed items (lost profits, loss of business, loss of data, punitive/special/incidental) so there's less semantic fight.

3) If DataStream insists on mutuality, we would need a cap increase (we typically cap liability at the greater of $1M or 2x fees; mutual consequential exclusion + no other concessions increases our risk model).

Laura — tagging you for legal redline text and any issues with the SLA carve-out. Marissa — can you confirm whether a cap increase to 3x fees or $3M is approvable from an ARR/discount perspective for this account? DataStream is at the cusp of committing to Dedicated capacity (this deal has expansion potential).

Thanks,
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai | +1 415 555 0198

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@datastrm.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — consequential damages / mutuality

Vivek / Marissa / Sarah —

Appreciate the context. Below are two redline options (text blocks you can drop into the MSA). My goal is to remove ambiguity and limit litigation-through-language while explaining the commercial compromises.

Option A (preferred for Redwood — one-way exclusion with precise carve-outs):

  "Neither party shall be liable to the other for any consequential, incidental, special, exemplary or punitive damages, including, without limitation, lost profits, loss of business, loss of data, or loss of customers, arising out of or relating to this Agreement; provided, however, that the foregoing exclusion shall not apply to (i) damages resulting from a party's gross negligence or willful misconduct; (ii) damages arising from a breach of Section [Confidentiality]; (iii) damages resulting from a party's failure to perform its obligations under an applicable Service Level Agreement set forth in an Order Form; or (iv) damages for which a party is required to indemnify the other under Section [IP Indemnity]."

Rationale: The SLA carve-out incentivizes both parties to agree clear operational metrics; it also provides a path to recover direct business impact tied to measurable infra failures.

Option B (DataStream's proposal but with a business-side concession):

  "Mutual Exclusion": Replace Section with a mutual exclusion as proposed by DataStream, and the parties agree that Redwood's aggregate liability cap shall be increased to the greater of $3,000,000 or three (3) times the fees paid by Customer in the prior 12 months.

Rationale: Mutuality transfers downstream systemic risk back to Redwood; if DataStream wants that allocation, we need commensurate pricing/limit changes.

Drafting notes on definition of consequential: I recommend keeping the enumerated list (lost profits, loss of business, loss of data, punitive, special, incidental) and avoid a catch-all definition referencing foreseeability. Enumeration reduces ambiguity and litigation cycles.

If DataStream accepts Option A, Laura will prepare a clean redline and we can move straight to order-form SLA definitions. If they insist on mutuality, we'll need to route to finance for cap update approval and update commercial terms.

——
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Compliance
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Sarah —

Thanks — quick commercial recap and ask so we can close this week.

Summary of Redwood's proposal:
- Redwood prefers a one-way exclusion but will accept precise carve-outs for (i) gross negligence/willful misconduct; (ii) breach of confidentiality; (iii) SLA failures per the Order Form; and (iv) IP indemnity.
- Redwood will enumerate consequential categories (lost profits, loss of business, loss of data, punitive/special/incidental) to avoid definition fights.
- If DataStream requires mutuality, Redwood requests a liability cap increase to the greater of $3,000,000 or 3x prior 12 months' fees.

Ask: Can DataStream confirm which path they prefer (Option A: one-way + carve-outs; Option B: mutual + cap increase) by end of day Friday? If Option A, we will circulate a redline (MSA-Redline-v3.pdf) that includes the SLA carve-out placeholder and an Order Form template for SLA metrics. If Option B, please confirm you accept the updated cap so we can surface to finance for sign-off.

I can also schedule a 20-minute call with Laura and Vivek if you prefer to walk through the language live.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
